Currently mathlib defines Abelian varieties as follows:

open AlgebraicGeometry CategoryTheory

variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}}

--Abelian Variety:
variable (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [IsProper G.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral G.hom] [GrpObj G]

Is there a reason why GrpObj G was chosen? Wouldn't it be better to go with AddGroupObj G? The reason I ask is because the endomorphism ring of an Abelian variety is mathematically very important, and writing f + g for the binary operation between two endomorphisms looks wrong when G is a GrpObj.
Would it make sense to change it to AddGrpObj?
Can we get @[to_additive] to work for this?
As of recently, you should write Spec ↧K instead of Spec (.of K).
What do you mean by "mathlib defines"? This is just a variable statement. You are free to change it as required

Thomas Browning said:

Can we get @[to_additive] to work for this?

You mean use GrpObj for the abelian variety. But, when defining the endomorphisms ring, switch using @[to_additive] (I am rather new to this, and although I have seen @[to_additive] in a couple of places, I am not sure how it works - so what I have written might be silly)?

Yaël Dillies said:

What do you mean by "mathlib defines"? This is just a variable statement. You are free to change it as required

Well, Mathlib hasn't defined abelian varieties yet. Although it has shown properties of it (i.e., that it is abelian), just using variables. And, there they use the multiplicative definition.

@[to_additive] is just a way of autogenerating additive declarations from multiplicative ones. So you state all of your theorems about abelian varieties multiplicatively, and then @[to_additive] will autogenerate the additive versions of those declarations.

When it comes time to defining the endomorphism ring, you might restrict to the case of additive abelian varieties, but then any theorems that you need will there because they will have been autogenerated by @[to_additive].

Thomas Browning said:

When it comes time to defining the endomorphism ring, you might restrict to the case of additive abelian varieties, but then any theorems that you need will there because they will have been autogenerated by @[to_additive].

Thanks! This was basically what has been bothering me after some other discussion I had over the endomorphism ring. This is very helpful, thanks a lot!

Abhijit A J said:

Well, Mathlib hasn't defined abelian varieties yet. Although it has shown properties of it (i.e., that it is abelian), just using variables

Mathlib never will define abelian varieties, because there is no consensus on what a variety is mathematically.

Abhijit A J said:

And, there they use the multiplicative definition.

That is a valid complaint. You could indeed use @[to_additive] there

@Yaël Dillies Haha. The first part is unfortunately so true! :sweat_smile:

A question about the second part (and this is where my lack of knowledge about @[to_additive] shows) - should the code in Mathlib/AlgebraicGeoemetry/Group/Abelian.lean be edited for this? That is, should it be added on there, or should I just do it in my own code. In which which case, how would I go about giving this instance:

theorem isCommAddMonObj_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral
    (G : Over (Spec ↧K)) [IsProper G.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral G.hom] [AddGrpObj G] :
    IsCommAddMonObj G := sorry

There is already a theorem/instance like this for the multiplicative case in the file I mentioned above.

Ideally you could tag docs#AlgebraicGeometry.isCommMonObj_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral with @[to_additive] and it would generate this theorem. But IIRC, it does not work right now. This should be fixed though.
(There may just be missing @[to_additive]s on the declarations used in the proof.)

This will be a tough robustness case for the to_additive attribute. (When you added this great theorem, I had secretly tried to add the to_additive attribute, and it had failed! I hope it is not trying to additivisize the multiplication on the sheaf of rings of the scheme!)

Yaël Dillies said:

Mathlib never will define abelian varieties, because there is no consensus on what a variety is mathematically.

It is true that there is no consensus on variety, but there is a consensus on abelian variety so this is not an objection.

Recently I heard that group theorists have no concensus on what a "finite group of Lie type" is, but they do have a concensus on what a "finite simple group of Lie type" is, which is good because such a phrase (which is still not formalised in mathlib or perhaps anywhere) shows up in the statement of the classification of finite simple groups.

Interesting. I was wondering if mathlib would indeed accept having an AbelianVariety definition on the basis that this is agreed-upon in the literature, or reject it on the basis that the style of the algebraic geometry library is to unbundle all assumptions.

I had secretly tried to add the to_additive attribute, and it had failed!

There's #42400 for better to_additive error message that might help diagnosing ...
